nodes.title: Proper smooth de Rham comparison and Hodge–Tate weights
nodes.statement: Let X/K be a proper smooth rigid space, i≥0, and Vᶦ=Hᶦ_et(X_C,Q_p). There is a natural G_K-equivariant strict filtered B_dR-isomorphism Vᶦ⊗B_dR ≅ Hᶦ_dR(X/K)⊗_K B_dR, with trivial filtration on Vᶦ and the tensor Hodge/period filtration on the right. Thus Vᶦ is de Rham, D_dR(Vᶦ)≅Hᶦ_dR(X/K) as filtered K-spaces, the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at E₁, and C⊗Vᶦ≅⊕_a C(−a)⊗_K H^{i−a}(X,Ω^a). In particular gr^a D_dR≅H^{i−a}(X,Ω^a) and weight −a occurs with that dimension. The same statements hold for proper smooth schemes after the algebraic/analytic comparison.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Instantiate P8/de-rham-comparison-for-de-rham-lisse-sheaves with the constant Q_p-sheaf and (O_X,d) with its trivial filtration. Scholze Remark 7.12 identifies its graded de Rham complex with Ω^a[−a]. This uses the existing comparison morphism, not a second construction of period sheaves.

The P8 comparison is strict and G_K-equivariant. Take invariants using B_dR^{G_K}=K and the dimension bound of R06.2; its inverse identifies the full Hodge filtration. The degeneration and C-decomposition are conclusions of the same P8 theorem, rather than deductions from an arbitrary unfiltered isomorphism.
For a scheme, use H5 algebraic/analytic étale comparison and coherent/de Rham GAGA. Pullback is induced by the natural maps in P8.
acceptance: X=Spec K, i=0 gives Q_p, D_dR=K, Fil⁰=K, Fil¹=0 and weight 0.
X=P¹, i=2 gives Q_p(−1), one jump at 1 and weight −1; it is not Q_p(1).
A proper smooth genus-g curve has weights 0 and −1, each g; no good-reduction hypothesis is needed.

nodes.title: Crystalline periods of a smooth proper model
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛/O_K be a proper smooth scheme or p-adic formal scheme, with smooth proper generic fibre X. For every i≥0, Vᶦ=Hᶦ_et(X_C,Q_p) is crystalline and D_cris(Vᶦ)≅Hᶦ_cris(𝔛_k/W(k))[1/p], preserving σ-semilinear φ. The underlying B_cris-comparison is G_K-equivariant. Tensoring with K gives D_dR(Vᶦ)≅Hᶦ_dR(X/K); its filtration is the Hodge filtration under Berthelot–Ogus. Hence gr^a D_dR≅H^{i−a}(X,Ω^a) and the Hodge–Tate weights lie in [−i,0]. No bound i<p−1, unramifiedness of K, or torsion-freeness of integral crystalline cohomology is assumed. This is a rational statement.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Combine AI.5/global-acrys and global-etale over B_cris with AI.5/rational-crystalline-frobenius, the residue-field bridge of BMS §13.21. The bridge is not by itself the crystalline comparison: composing the three actual maps is the assembly moved here from CP.2.

Functoriality of AΩ and the residue bridge supplies G_K- and φ-equivariance. For schemes first pass to their p-adic formal completion and use H5. Take invariants using B_cris^{G_K}=K₀; equality of period ranks gives crystallinity.

The B_dR-extension of this assembly is the proper smooth de Rham comparison, by BMS Theorem 14.6 and the existing AI.6 smooth comparison agreement. Identify the crystalline-to-de Rham map with Berthelot–Ogus, then apply the preceding node to its filtration and gradeds.
acceptance: For P¹ and i=2, D_cris(Q_p(−1)) has φ=p and Hodge jump 1.
For an abelian scheme, i=1 gives rank 2g; dualizing changes both φ and filtration as in the next application.
The rational theorem applies to p=2 and to arbitrary i; it does not identify an integral lattice when special-fibre crystalline cohomology has torsion.

nodes.title: Proper semistable periods and Hyodo–Kato realization
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be proper p-adic formal over O_K, with the divisorial log structure, and an étale affine cover with étale maps to Spf(O_K{t₀,…,t_d}/(t₀⋯t_r−a)) for nonzero nonunits a∈O_K; a may vary between charts. Put X=𝔛_η and Hᶦ_HK=Hᶦ_logcrys(𝔛_k/W(k))[1/p] over the standard log point ℕ→W(k), 1↦0. There is a natural G_K-equivariant B_st-comparison Hᶦ_et(X_C,Q_p)⊗B_st≅Hᶦ_HK⊗_{K₀}B_st preserving φ and total N=N_HK⊗1+1⊗N_Bst. Thus Vᶦ is semistable and D_st(Vᶦ)≅Hᶦ_HK as (φ,N)-modules. With the fixed embedding B_st→B_dR, its extension agrees with the preceding de Rham comparison, and K⊗D_st carries the Hodge filtration via the compatible Hyodo–Kato map. Use the period-normalized HK monodromy: raw uniformizer monodromy is adjusted under the CR.6 ramification normalization. Smooth reduction is the N=0 crystalline case. The statement also applies to schemes satisfying these model hypotheses.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Use AI.6/hyodo-kato-interface over B_st⁺, including arithmetic W(k)-descent and total monodromy; then invert μ and apply AI.6/etale-comparison. This is exactly the rational assembly in CK Theorem 9.5. Neither the integral AΩ complex nor the log site is rebuilt here.

CR.6 supplies finite-dimensional HK cohomology and its φ,N. Check its monodromy convention against CK §9.1: N_Bst(log[p̃])=−1. A log base change of ramification index e scales raw monodromy; use CR.6/ramified-hk-base-change to divide by e before comparing with the p-normalized period operator. This check is part of the named supplier contract.

Take G_K-invariants using B_st^{G_K}=K₀ and the dimension bound. AI.6/etale-bdr-agreement (CK Proposition 6.8) identifies the B_dR-extension with the strict filtered de Rham comparison. Changes of uniformizer act through CR.6/uniformizer-change and its compatible period embedding; no choice-free filtration on B_st is asserted.
acceptance: A smooth proper model gives N=0 and the preceding crystalline realization.
A split Tate elliptic curve gives a nonzero rank-one N in H¹, and dualizing it gives the Tate module computed in R06.6; an N=0 substitute fails.
After a ramified extension of degree e, raw uniformizer N scales by e, but the period-normalized realization is the scalar extension of the original one.

For a Tate curve over a field of ramification index e, CR.6 raw cohomological N(e₁)=v_K(q)e₀ becomes (v_K(q)/e)e₀. In the dual of the covariant period basis, map e₀ to −y* and e₁ to x*: N(x*)=−v_p(q)y*. The sign and the divisor e are both necessary.

nodes.title: Potential semistability without a semistable model hypothesis
nodes.statement: For X/K proper smooth rigid (or a proper smooth scheme), every Vᶦ=Hᶦ_et(X_C,Q_p) is potentially semistable. There is a finite Galois L/K such that dim_{L₀}D_st,L(Vᶦ)=dim_Qp Vᶦ, and D_pst(Vᶦ) is the scalar extension of this module to K₀^{nr} with its semilinear G_K-descent action. If X_L has a proper semistable model of the preceding kind, the semistable node identifies D_st,L with that model’s normalized HK cohomology and transports its filtration. Different such models or splitting fields give the same period object and descent data. This assertion does not posit a finite semistable model for every proper rigid space, nor does it assert semistability over K.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply the proper smooth de Rham node, then R06.3/p-adic-monodromy-theorem. Enlarge a finite splitting extension to its Galois closure using R06.2 base change.

Use the existing R06.3 potential-period/descent construction, independent of the finite splitting extension, to obtain D_pst. If a semistable model is available, apply the preceding comparison over L; its identification is canonical through D_st,L and compatible with further extensions.

Colmez–Nizioł Theorem 6.4 proves a stronger analytic HK period comparison. Only its potential-admissibility consequence is needed here. The full analytic HK construction and its syntomic/descent proof are not silently substituted for the model-based CR.6 input.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve with potentially good additive reduction, V_p becomes crystalline after extension but need not be semistable over K.
A ramified quadratic twist of a Tate curve is potentially semistable with nonzero N; it is not potentially crystalline.
Replacing L by a larger finite Galois field preserves rank and descends to the same D_pst.

nodes.title: Geometric functoriality, cohomological duals and Tate twists
nodes.statement: The preceding rational comparison maps commute with pullback between the indicated proper smooth spaces/models, with cup products, and with finite base extension. For an algebraic proper smooth geometrically connected X/K of pure dimension d, the perfect pairing Hᶦ_et(X_Kbar,Q_p)×H^{2d−i}_et(X_Kbar,Q_p)(d)→Q_p induces Vᶦ∨≅V^{2d−i}(d). For B=B_dR, and B=B_cris or B_st under the corresponding model hypothesis, D_B(V∨(m))≅D_B(V)∨⊗D_B(Q_p(m)). Thus D_cris(Q_p(m)) has φ=p^{−m}σ and N=0, the de Rham filtration shifts by −m, and Hodge–Tate weights shift by +m. Under the geometric comparisons the dual pairing is the transported geometric cohomological pairing. A G_K-equivariant cohomological projector that also acts on the matched geometric realization can be applied to the comparisons; admissibility, filtration and φ,N restrict to its image. A compatible system alone does not provide such a projector.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Naturality follows from the actual P8/AInf maps. Cup compatibility is carried through their multiplicative period-sheaf/AΩ morphisms and CR.6/hk-products; it is requested explicitly where those supplier nodes do not yet state it.

Import rational étale Poincaré duality from EDC.2:pairings/adic-and-rational-poincare-duality. Apply the already monoidal, dual-compatible R06.2 period functors to its evaluation and coevaluation maps, obtaining the displayed dual identification. This transports a pairing without requiring a new independently defined crystalline trace.

R06.2 gives the period line of Q_p(m) and the dual filtration Fil^rD∨={λ:λ(Fil^{1−r}D)=0}. The geometric comparison identifies the transported pairing with cup product and the normalized top-degree Tate line; a cycle/trace normalization is an explicit supplier contract. An idempotent commutes with a natural comparison when its action has been supplied on both sides; then use exactness on admissible representations.
acceptance: For P¹, V²=Q_p(−1) and V⁰(1)=Q_p(1) are dual; twisting H² by 1 removes its Hodge jump and Frobenius p.
For a curve, H¹∨≅H¹(1); for V_p(A)=H¹∨ the weights change from {0,−1} to {0,1}.
The identity and zero projectors give the entire realization and the zero space. An ℓ-adic polynomial match without a geometric operator does not imply a p-adic filtered projector.

nodes.title: The covariant crystalline realization of an abelian scheme
nodes.statement: Let 𝔄/O_K be an abelian scheme of relative dimension g with fibres A/K and A₀/k. Write V_p(A)=T_p(A)⊗Q_p, covariantly. Then D_cris(V_p(A))≅H¹_cris(A₀/W(k))[1/p]∨ with inverse-dual σ-semilinear Frobenius. Over K its filtered realization is H¹_dR(A/K)∨; Fil⁰ is the annihilator of H⁰(A,Ω¹), canonically H¹(A,O_A)∨, and gr^{−1}≅H⁰(A,Ω¹)∨≅Lie(A). Both graded ranks are g, the weights are 0 and 1, and t_H=t_N=−g. The integral crystalline H¹ is identified with the Frobenius pullback of the contravariant Dieudonné module of A₀[p^∞] by the imported degree-one comparison; that pullback is retained until its semilinear convention has been matched. No integral equality with the dual Tate lattice follows from this rational statement.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: A4/realization-conventions gives V_p(A)=H¹_et(A_Kbar,Q_p)∨. Apply the crystalline comparison, then the dual-compatible R06.2 functor. Frobenius on a dual is the inverse transpose, not the transpose.
Dualize A4/abelian-h1-de-rham: 0→H⁰Ω¹→H¹_dR→H¹O→0. Use the dual filtration formula to obtain Fil⁰ and gr^{−1}, and weak admissibility to compute t_N=t_H=−g.

Import the H¹_cris/contravariant Dieudonné comparison from R07.2/A4 pd-first-cohomology. Brinon–Conrad Remark 7.3.3 uses a σ-pullback; an identification omitting it must provide its explicit semilinear untwisting. Its Fontaine–Honda discussion over unramified K is not used to restrict the geometric comparison to that case.
acceptance: For g=0 the realization is zero and t_H=t_N=0.
For a good ordinary elliptic curve the covariant slopes are −1 and 0; for a supersingular one they are −1/2,−1/2.
For a product A×B the dimensions and t_H add. A polarization of degree divisible by p still gives rational duality, without an integral perfect pairing.

nodes.title: Abelian Tate modules are de Rham of weights zero and one
nodes.statement: For every abelian variety A/K of dimension g, without a reduction hypothesis, V_p(A) is de Rham and D_dR(V_p(A))≅H¹_dR(A/K)∨ with filtration jumps −1 and 0 of multiplicity g. There is a natural G_K-equivariant Hodge–Tate decomposition C⊗V_p(A)≅(C(1)⊗_K Lie(A))⊕(C⊗_K H¹(A,O_A)∨). Consequently its Hodge–Tate weights are 0 and 1, each g. The rational statement is independent of a choice of good or semistable model.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply the proper smooth de Rham comparison to A, then A4/realization-conventions and dual compatibility. Properness and smoothness are supplied by the existing abelian-variety carrier and A4 realization.
The Hodge exact sequence of A4 has two rank-g terms. Dualize it using Fil⁰=ann(Fil¹), and dualize the canonical C-decomposition from the de Rham comparison; H⁰Ω¹∨=Lie(A).
Read the sign using R06.2/hodge-tate-weight-convention: a jump −1 contributes +1. This proof does not invoke the good-reduction criterion and hence cannot form a cycle with it.
acceptance: The zero abelian variety has no weights.
A Tate elliptic curve has weights 0 and 1 despite N≠0; these weights alone do not force crystallinity.
Good ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves have the same two weights; Frobenius slopes distinguish them instead.

nodes.title: Period realization of the Weil pairing
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A/K, the Weil pairing yields V_p(A^∨)≅V_p(A)∨(1). A polarization λ gives a nondegenerate alternating pairing V_p(A)×V_p(A)→Q_p(1); its integral version on T_p(A) is perfect when p∤deg λ. Applying D_dR, or D_cris/D_st when admissible, gives the corresponding perfect filtered pairing into the rank-one period line of Q_p(1). That line has φ=p^{−1}σ, N=0 and a single jump at −1. Thus for g=1, det D_cris(V_p(A)) is that line; if k=F_{p^f}, det(φ^f)=p^{−f}. In dimension g, det(φ^f)=p^{−fg}. The rational determinant character det V_p(A)=Q_p(g) is imported from arithmetic Tate theory, rather than defined again here.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Import the finite Weil pairing and its compatible inverse limit from A3 and R01.6/arithmetic-polarized-pairing. For elliptic curves current Tau Ceti already defines the Tate pairing and proves its determinant character; this part supplies their period realizations.
Use the tensor/dual period functors and the period Tate line. Evaluate the pairing on determinant top exterior powers, or import R01.6/tate-determinant-character and then apply D_cris.
Only φ^f is K₀-linear when f>1. For integral perfectness restrict to p∤deg λ; after tensoring Q_p every polarization is invertible, so rational perfectness has no such restriction.
acceptance: For g=1 over Q_p, det φ=p^{−1}, not p; the latter belongs to cohomological H¹.
For g=2 over F_{p²}, det(φ²)=p^{−4}; using p^{−2} confuses dimension or residue degree.
A polarization with p dividing its degree can have a degenerate mod-p pairing even though its rational period pairing is perfect.

nodes.title: Good ordinary and supersingular elliptic realizations
nodes.statement: Let E/K have good reduction E₀/F_q, q=p^f, and let a=q+1−#E₀(F_q). The rank-two D=D_cris(V_p(E)) has filtration jumps −1,0 and det(X−φ^f|D)=X²−(a/q)X+1/q. If p∤a, E₀ is ordinary: D has slopes −1,0 and its slope −1 submodule is weakly admissible, giving a G_K-stable Q_p(1) times unramified character line in V_p(E). If p|a, E₀ is supersingular: D has slopes −1/2,−1/2, no rank-one φ-stable K₀-submodule, and V_p(E) is irreducible over Q_p. This is not absolute irreducibility after enlarging coefficient fields. φ^f may be scalar when f>1 without producing a φ-stable line.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply the abelian-scheme realization. Import the common finite-field H¹ Frobenius polynomial from the lower-tier crystalline/étale Frobenius comparison; dualize φ^f to obtain the displayed reciprocal polynomial.

Use R07.2 height-two Dieudonné/isocrystal classification: ordinary has slopes 0,1 on H¹, supersingular has 1/2,1/2. The Hasse bound and the trace alone are not the proof of the slope assertion over every F_{p^f}.

In the ordinary case weak admissibility forces Fil⁰D_K not to equal the slope −1 line: otherwise that line would have t_H=0>−1=t_N. Its induced jump is −1 and it is weakly admissible. Full faithfulness/exactness of admissible period functors gives the Galois subrepresentation.

A rank-one σ-isocrystal over the unramified K₀ has integral slope: write φ(e)=b e, and v_p(det φ^f)=f v_p(b) with v_p(b)∈Z. Thus a half-slope rank-two object has no φ-stable K₀-line. Any Q_p subrepresentation would supply one.
acceptance: Over F₅, y²=x³+x has #E=4 and a=2; the reciprocal polynomial is X²−(2/5)X+1/5 and the two slopes are −1,0.
Over F₃, y²=x³−x has #E=4 and a=0; its slopes are both −1/2 and V₃ is Q₃-irreducible.
Base-change the latter curve to F₉: φ² on its covariant isocrystal is scalar −1/3. Nevertheless φ is semilinear and there is still no K₀ φ-stable line.

nodes.title: Kummer lattices and rational extensions
nodes.statement: For q∈K× choose compatible p-power roots q_n in Kbar with q₀=q, and compatible primitive roots ε_n with ε₀=1. For g∈G_K, g(q_n)/q_n=ε_n^{c_q(g) mod p^n} defines a continuous c_q:G_K→Z_p(1), with coordinates c_q(gh)=c_q(g)+χ_p(g)c_q(h). On the existing rank-two Z_p-module let T(q)=Z_p e⊕Z_p f with g(e)=χ_p(g)e and g(f)=f+c_q(g)e; let V(q)=Q_p⊗T(q). It is an extension 0→Q_p(1)→V(q)→Q_p→0 with Kummer class δ(q). Changes of roots change c_q by a coboundary. Import the completed multiplicative module K̂×=lim K×/(K×)^{p^n} from LocalGaloisGroups Layer 7; its rationalization maps isomorphically to H¹_cont(G_K,Q_p(1)) and hence to this continuous representation Ext¹. The pair (v_p,log_K) identifies it with Q_p⊕K. V(q) splits iff q is a root of unity. Integrally, T(q) splits iff q∈∩_n(K×)^{p^n}, which for finite K is the subgroup of roots of unity of order prime to p; nontrivial p-power roots can survive as torsion Kummer classes. No action of all ring automorphisms of Kbar is used: G_K fixes q.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: At each finite level use the pinned TauCeti.kummerCocycle and kummerCocycle_mem_Z1, with the actual K-algebra Galois action and the same root choices. The finite cocycle classes agree under transition maps; the continuous inverse-limit dictionary in R02.1 identifies their limit with H¹_cont(G_K,Z_p(1)).

The cocycle equation is exactly the upper-right entry of the multiplication law for [[χ,c],[0,1]]. Invertibility follows from χ∈Z_p× and continuity from its two entries. Interpret the action as Mathlib Representation on the existing free module; a separate KummerCocycle carrier is unnecessary.

Changing q_n by ε_n^b changes the coordinate cocycle by (χ−1)b. Conjugation by a unipotent matrix gives an isomorphism of extensions. Tensor the completed Kummer map with Q_p, using the imported valuation/principal-unit logarithm calculation, to obtain Q_p⊕K.

LocalGaloisGroups separates finite p-power torsion from the free completed module. Its image vanishes rationally but may be nonzero integrally. The free part is detected by valuation and log, so rational splitting occurs exactly for roots of unity. This is the correction to the checkpoint’s integral root-of-unity test.

nodes.title: The semistable period basis of a Kummer extension
nodes.statement: Every continuous extension of Q_p by Q_p(1) over G_K is semistable. For V(q) there is u_q∈B_st⁺ with g(u_q)=u_q+c_q(g)t, φ(u_q)=p u_q, N(u_q)=−v_p(q), and image u_q in B_dR giving log_K(q) modulo the filtration. In the invariant basis x=t^{−1}e, y=−u_q t^{−1}e+f of D_st(V(q)), one has φ(x)=p^{−1}x, φ(y)=y, N(x)=0, N(y)=v_p(q)x. The Hodge filtration is Fil^{−1}=D_K, Fil⁰=K(y+log_K(q)x), Fil¹=0. Thus t_H=t_N=−1, and V(q) is crystalline iff v_p(q)=0. The logarithm branch is log_K(p)=0; changing the branch changes the period embedding and the filtration coordinates together.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Build u_q from the compatible roots using R06.1/crystalline-logarithm and the semistable logarithm variable. Its Galois and Frobenius transformations make x,y invariant; their independence yields full period rank. N=−d/du gives the positive sign in N(y).
Embed into B_dR with log_K(p)=0; u_q−log_K(q) belongs to Fil¹, so y+log_K(q)x belongs to Fil⁰. The line and jumps follow by dimension and the underlying Q_p(1),Q_p extension.

For general H¹(Q_p(1)) classes use the rationalized completed Kummer isomorphism: every class is a finite Q_p-linear combination of classes of elements of K×. Baer sums are subquotients of direct sums of their semistable representations; the category is closed under direct sums and subquotients. This does not assert that arbitrary extensions of semistable representations are semistable.
The crystalline subspace is ker N=D_cris(V); it has full rank precisely when v_p(q)=0. Read filtration and determinant to get t_H=t_N=−1.
acceptance: q=p gives φ=diag(p^{−1},1), N(y)=x and Fil⁰=Ky: semistable, nonsplit, noncrystalline.
For p odd and q=1+p, valuation is zero but log_K(q)≠0; the representation is crystalline and nonsplit.
For a root of unity, both coordinates vanish and V(q)=Q_p(1)⊕Q_p; integral torsion can remain as in the construction test.

nodes.title: The p-adic Tate lattice of a Tate curve
nodes.statement: For q∈K× with 0<|q|<1, import the Tate curve E_q and the G_K-equivariant uniformization Kbar×/q^Z≅E_q(Kbar), compatible over finite extensions. At level p^n, the classes ε_n^i q_n^j with 0≤i,j<p^n are exactly E_q[p^n], each occurring once. Their multiplication-by-p transitions give a G_K-equivariant isomorphism T_p(E_q)≅T(q), compatible with the injection Z_p(1) and quotient Z_p, and hence V_p(E_q)≅V(q). The extension class is the Kummer class of q. This is the residue-characteristic p adapter; R01.6 already owns the analogous ℓ≠p arithmetic statement.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply the imported analytic uniformization at each finite extension containing the finite torsion. A class z modulo q^Z is p^n-torsion iff z^{p^n}=q^j for some j; reducing j modulo p^n gives the displayed representatives and uniqueness.
Compute multiplication by p on these representatives using q_{n+1}^p=q_n and ε_{n+1}^p=ε_n. Transition maps are surjective, and the inverse-limit basis is (ε_n),(q_n).

The G_K action on the first basis vector is χ_p and on the second is the Kummer cocycle from the preceding construction. The finite-level exact sequences therefore give precisely its lattice, including the extension class.
acceptance: At level p^n the count is p^{2n}, not (p^n−1)²; both index endpoints are <p^n.
The roots of unity supply the Z_p(1) sublattice, rather than the trivial quotient.
Replacing q by q^p multiplies the extension class by p: the rational representations are isomorphic, but the natural isogeny need not identify integral lattices.

nodes.title: The filtered Frobenius–monodromy module of a Tate curve
nodes.statement: For 0<|q|<1 put v=v_p(q)>0 and ℓ=log_K(q). Then V_p(E_q) is semistable and noncrystalline, with D_st basis x,y satisfying φ=diag(p^{−1},1) semilinearly, N(y)=v x, N(x)=0, and Fil⁰D_K=K(y+ℓx), Fil^{−1}=D_K, Fil¹=0. N has rank one and remains nonzero after every finite extension, so E_q is not potentially good and V_p(E_q) is not potentially crystalline or potentially Barsotti–Tate. It is ordinary with weights 0,1 and t_H=t_N=−1. Over Q_p the arithmetic WD Frobenius is diag(p,1) in this basis and satisfies F N F^{−1}=pN; the convention with geometric Frobenius uses p^{−1}.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Identify V_p(E_q) with V(q), then apply its explicit period calculation. Positivity of v gives rank-one N.

The only nonzero proper φ,N-stable line is K₀x; its induced filtration has the jump −1, so its t_H=t_N=−1. The full object also has equality; this is the weak-admissibility check, not a proof for all arbitrary filtrations.

R06.2 finite base change preserves the normalized nonzero monodromy. Good iff crystalline below, and R07.4’s crystalline weights-0,1 lattice criterion, rule out potential good reduction and potential Barsotti–Tate.
Apply the already planned R06.3 Tate WD convention. At K=Q_p its arithmetic F=φ^{−1}; conjugating the upper-right N entry multiplies it by p.
acceptance: q=p has ℓ=0 but N(y)=x≠0. A zero L-invariant does not mean good reduction.
For q=p^m and m≥1, N(y)=m x and Fil⁰=Ky; φ,N,fil satisfy Nφ=pφN.
After a ramified extension the raw integer valuation grows, but normalized N stays nonzero; an argument declaring it zero after extension is invalid.

nodes.title: The normalized Tate L-invariant
nodes.statement: Use the existing weakly admissible filtered (φ,N)-module carrier of R06.2. A Tate-type object here is a rank-two D over K₀ with a one-dimensional Q_p-space D^{φ=1}, generated by y, such that N(y)≠0, φ(Ny)=p^{−1}Ny, and y,Ny span D. Its Hodge filtration has Fil^{−1}=D_K, Fil¹=0 and a one-dimensional Fil⁰ transverse to ker N. Define L(D)∈K by Fil⁰D_K=K(y+L(D)Ny). This is independent of the choice of nonzero y∈D^{φ=1}. For the Kummer normal form with v_p(q)≠0, L(V(q))=log_K(q)/v_p(q). Two such unframed filtered (φ,N)-modules are isomorphic iff their L-invariants agree; by the existing admissible equivalence, the corresponding rational representations are isomorphic iff the invariants agree. The statement concerns this exact Tate-type class, not arbitrary semistable rank-two objects or framed extension classes.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Weak admissibility forces Fil⁰≠ker N because the slope −1 line would otherwise have t_H=0>t_N=−1. Decompose a generator of Fil⁰ in the basis (Ny,y); its y coefficient is nonzero, so normalize it to 1.

Every other φ-fixed generator is a Q_p× multiple of y and scales Ny by the same factor. This proves independence. In the basis (x,y) with Ny=v x and Fil⁰=K(y+ℓx), the coefficient relative to Ny is ℓ/v.

A φ,N isomorphism scales y and Ny together and hence preserves L. Conversely mapping these canonical bases with the same L preserves all structures. For normal forms (v,ℓ),(v′,ℓ′), a diagonal map x↦αx′, y↦βy′ works exactly when vα=βv′ and ℓα=βℓ′.
The branch change log′(p)=b adds b v_p(q) to ℓ, hence adds b to L; its comparison uses the corresponding changed period embedding. This is not invariance under an unrecorded logarithm choice.
acceptance: q=p has L=0 and remains noncrystalline.
Replacing q by q^a, a≠0, scales (v,ℓ) together and leaves L fixed.
Using raw log_K(q) instead of the quotient fails the isogeny test q↦q² whenever log_K(q)≠0.

nodes.title: The p-adic good-reduction criterion
nodes.statement: An abelian variety A/K has good reduction iff V_p(A) is crystalline, for every p including 2 and every finite K/Q_p. Equivalently, its covariant rational Tate representation is crystalline of weights 0,1. A has potentially good reduction iff V_p(A) is potentially crystalline; since this representation is always de Rham and potentially semistable, this is also equivalent to N=0 on D_pst(V_p(A)). For a minimal Weierstrass model this agrees with Mathlib WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction. No good reduction over K is inferred from crystallinity only after extension.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Good reduction gives an abelian O_K-model by Néron R11.1. Apply the abelian-scheme crystalline realization; it works without a ramification bound.

Conversely V_p(A) has weights 0,1 by the arbitrary-reduction de Rham node. Use R07.4/crystalline-01-is-bt in its lattice form: the actual stable lattice T_p(A) comes from a p-divisible group G/O_K, not just a rational isogeny class.

At every n, G[p^n](Kbar)≅T_p(A)/p^n≅A[p^n](Kbar), compatibly in n. The finite étale generic-fibre/Galois-module equivalence identifies G_K with A[p^∞] over K. Invoke the requested Grothendieck compatible finite-flat model criterion in Néron R11.3 (Brinon–Conrad Theorem 7.1.13) to get good reduction. An unrelated finite flat model at one level would not suffice.

Apply the equivalence over finite extensions to obtain potential good iff potential crystalline. On a finite semistable splitting extension, D_cris=ker N in D_st; full rank is equivalent to N=0. Use R06.3 descent for independence of the splitting field.
acceptance: A good supersingular elliptic curve is crystalline although its rational Tate representation is irreducible.
A split Tate curve is semistable with N≠0 and fails both good and potentially good reduction.
A potentially good curve with additive reduction need only become crystalline over an extension; the theorem does not claim its original representation is crystalline.

nodes.title: Semistable abelian reduction gives semistable periods
nodes.statement: If A/K has semistable reduction, V_p(A) is semistable. Every abelian variety acquires semistable reduction over a finite extension and hence has a potentially semistable rational Tate module. For the Raynaud uniformization A^an=G^an/Γ, with 0→T→G→B→0, its covariant Tate representation has a filtration V_p(T)⊂V_p(G)⊂V_p(A), with graded terms V_p(T), V_p(B), Γ⊗Q_p. B has good reduction and the actions on X_*(T) and Γ are unramified; the outer terms are unramified representations twisted by 1 and 0 respectively. They are crystalline, but their successive extensions need not be. For a semistable A, N=0 iff A has good reduction by the preceding criterion. This part does not claim the converse semistable-reduction criterion or the rank-N/toric-rank formula; their owner is Néron R11.4–R11.5.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Import Néron R11.3 Raynaud uniformization with its Galois descent and compatible exact torsion sequences. Inverse limits give the stated filtration; a merely ℓ≠p inertia filtration is insufficient for this step.

The unramified lattice and cocharacter actions give crystalline outer terms; the good-reduction theorem gives crystalline V_p(B). The entire V_p(A) and all its subquotients are de Rham by the arbitrary-reduction abelian node and the de Rham category’s closure properties.

Apply R06.4/ordinary-implies-semistable(a) twice: a de Rham extension of semistable representations is semistable. Alternatively split the unramified torus/lattice action over a finite unramified field and descend by R06.2. De Rham is an essential hypothesis; semistable representations are not asserted closed under all extensions.
Néron finite-separable-semistable-extension gives potential semistability. The N=0 criterion then uses good iff crystalline, not a downstream Néron period comparison.
acceptance: Good reduction has T=Γ=0 and recovers a crystalline representation.
A Tate curve has B=0 and two crystalline graded lines, but its extension has N≠0.
A nonsplit multiplicative curve has nontrivial unramified quadratic action on both graded lines and is still semistable over K.

nodes.title: Split, nonsplit and potentially multiplicative elliptic periods
nodes.statement: Let E/K be elliptic with v_p(j(E))<0. The imported Tate twist theorem supplies q∈K× with 0<|q|<1 and E≅E_q⊗η for a quadratic character η. E is split multiplicative iff η=1, nonsplit multiplicative iff η is nontrivial unramified, and additive potentially multiplicative iff η is ramified. Then V_p(E)≅V(q)⊗η. In the first two cases it is semistable with nonzero rank-one N; in the third it is potentially semistable with N≠0 and nontrivial inertial descent, but is not semistable over K. All three fail potential crystallinity and potential good reduction. For K=Q_p in the nonsplit case, D_st has φ=diag(−p^{−1},−1), N(y)=v_p(q)x and the same filtration normal form after choosing a generator of the unramified period line. The minimal-equation predicates agree with Mathlib HasMultiplicativeReduction and HasSplitMultiplicativeReduction.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Import the Tate j-parameter and quadratic twist classification from EllipticCurves Layer 4 (and its reduction algorithm). This node does not construct that curve or classify reduction again.

Tensor the Tate period realization by the finite character. An unramified η is crystalline of weight 0 and multiplies Frobenius by its unramified eigenvalue; at Q_p a nontrivial quadratic value is −1. The nilpotent N is unchanged up to the tensor line.

For ramified η, choose a finite splitting extension. Its WD inertial descent is η|I_K, and remains nontrivial even after Frobenius semisimplification. R06.3’s descent criterion for semistability excludes semistability over K; nonzero N excludes potential crystallinity.
Use a minimal Weierstrass equation when relating this conclusion to Mathlib predicates. A scaled nonminimal equation cannot test good or multiplicative reduction.
acceptance: E_q itself is the split case: determinant φ=p^{−1} and N≠0.
The unramified quadratic twist of E_p/Q_p is nonsplit multiplicative, has arithmetic WD F=diag(−p,−1), and remains semistable.
A ramified quadratic twist of E_p has nontrivial WD inertia and is not semistable over K, though its restriction to the splitting field is the Tate representation.

nodes.title: Coefficient-prime compatibility at good abelian reduction
nodes.statement: Let A/F be an abelian variety over a number field, v|p a good-reduction place, k_v=F_q and q=p^f. Let P_v(X)∈Z[X] be the common arithmetic Frobenius polynomial on V_ℓ(A), ℓ≠p, imported from R01.6. Then D_cris(H¹_et(A_Fbar,Q_p)|G_{F_v}) has charpolynomial det(X−φ^f)=P_v(X). On D_cris(V_p(A)) the eigenvalues of φ^f are their reciprocals. The arithmetic WD Frobenius is φ^{−f}, so det(X−F|WD_p(V_p(A)))=P_v(X), inertia is trivial and N=0. After Frobenius semisimplification and a common algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field, WD_p(V_p(A))≅WD_ℓ(V_ℓ(A)) for every ℓ≠p. This is deduced from the actual common reduction, not inferred for arbitrary almost strictly compatible systems. Endomorphisms and supplied projectors preserve this comparison only when they act compatibly on both realizations. The bad-place Tate-curve parameter is supplied by the preceding explicit nodes, not by its good-place polynomials.
hypotheses: The base field and period conventions below apply; additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: R01.6 supplies good reduction specialization and the integral Frobenius polynomial. Apply the abelian-scheme comparison to the good O_{F_v}-model and the lower-tier Katz–Messing crystalline/étale Frobenius theorem to H¹ of its projective special fibre.
Dualize to V_p(A) and invert φ^f as prescribed by the arithmetic WD convention of R06.3. The two inversions cancel, yielding P_v. Crystallinity gives trivial inertia and N=0.

The ℓ≠p representation is unramified with the same P_v. Over an algebraically closed coefficient field, equality of polynomials identifies the semisimple Frobenius operators and therefore their unramified Frobenius-semisimple WD representations. No stronger nonsemisimple claim follows from a polynomial alone.
For endomorphism summands use actual geometric functoriality on both sides, as above. A common rational polynomial on the whole space alone does not identify each coefficient-field factor.
acceptance: For y²+y=x³−x²−10x−20 (11a1) at p=3, #E(F₃)=5 and a₃=−1, so P₃=X²+X+3; the covariant D_cris polynomial is X²+X/3+1/3.
For P¹ in cohomological degree 2, crystalline φ^f has eigenvalue q; the covariant dual has eigenvalue q^{−1}, and arithmetic WD returns q.
For a split Tate curve over Q_p the bad-place arithmetic WD polynomial is (X−p)(X−1) and N≠0. Replacing it by a crystalline good-place parameter discards genuine monodromy.

The global crystalline/étale assembly is natural and multiplicative and normalizes the top cohomological Tate line on projective space. Supply these precise cup/line compatibilities for geometric duality and projector restrictions; this is not a general integral correspondence diagram.

State naturality and cup compatibility of the underlying semistable global crystalline, étale and HK maps, including their B_dR agreement after descent to K. The target geometric-period-functoriality-duality-twists assembles these maps; the old bdr-comparison-map target explicitly does not assert arbitrary-model naturality or multiplicativity. In addition to its p-divisible Dieudonné carrier, supply the degree-one contravariant comparison H¹_cris(A₀/W(k))≅D(A₀[p^∞])^{(p)} for abelian A₀/k, with its σ-pullback and explicit Frobenius convention. Supply height-two ordinary/supersingular slope classification over every finite residue field. The comparison is imported here; the unread proof is not reconstructed from a name search.
Good reduction means extension of A/K to an abelian scheme over O_K, equivalently its Néron model is abelian. For elliptic curves identify this with Mathlib’s minimal HasGoodReduction predicate.

Add Grothendieck’s p-divisible good-reduction criterion: A/K is good iff there are finite flat O_K-models G_n of A[p^n] with G_n=G_{n+1}[p^n] compatibly with generic fibres (equivalently A[p^∞] extends). For the existing Raynaud uniformization, state the G_K-equivariant compatible p^n-torsion exact sequences for T,G,B,Γ, and that X_*(T) and Γ have unramified action in the semistable case. These geometric contracts are needed before R11.5, which consumes the present period conclusions.

Use continuous cohomology for compact Z_p(1) and locally compact Q_p(1): the inverse-limit finite Kummer classes yield H¹_cont(G_K,Z_p(1))≅lim K×/(K×)^{p^n}; rationalization yields H¹_cont(G_K,Q_p(1)). Identify this H¹ with Ext¹ in continuous finite-dimensional Q_p representations and split iff zero, compatible with root changes and Baer sums. The discrete-module Ext dictionary in R02.4 is not sufficient.

Katz–Messing for smooth projective geometrically connected X/F_q: the characteristic polynomial of φ^f on rational crystalline Hᶦ equals that of geometric Frobenius on Hᶦ_et for every ℓ≠p. In degree one this is the arithmetic Frobenius polynomial on the covariant Tate module. Track f and dual inversions explicitly.
Use the existing finite Kummer isomorphism and local cohomology conventions as the inputs to the R02.1 continuous inverse-limit adapter. No reconstruction of local class field theory is requested.

The principal-unit p-adic logarithm, with kernel the roots of unity after rationalization, and the valuation/logarithm isomorphism Q_p⊗_{Z_p} padicCompletionUnits p K ≅ Q_p⊕K, v_p(p)=1 and log_K(p)=0. The completion itself is already owned by current LocalGaloisGroups Layer 7.

For 0<|q|<1 supply the existing Tate curve and the G_K-equivariant Kbar×/q^Z uniformization compatible over finite extensions, with its p-power torsion. For v(j(E))<0 supply the unique Tate parameter and quadratic twist: trivial iff split multiplicative, nontrivial unramified iff nonsplit multiplicative, ramified iff additive potentially multiplicative. Relate this to the minimal Mathlib reduction predicates. These are existing EllipticCurves targets; this part owns only their period adapter.

conventions.base: Fix a prime p, a finite extension K/Q_p, its algebraic closure Kbar and completion C, residue field k=F_(p^f), K0=W(k)[1/p], sigma the Witt Frobenius and G_K=Gal(Kbar/K). All representations are continuous and finite dimensional unless a lattice is named.
conventions.periods: Use covariant D_B(V)=(B tensor_Qp V)^(G_K). On B_st use N=-d/du and N phi=p phi N. Normalize v_p(p)=1 and log_K(p)=0. The filtration on K tensor_K0 D_st is transported through this specified embedding B_st into B_dR.
conventions.weights: HT(Q_p(1))=+1. Thus gr^a D_dR contributes weight -a; H^i_et of a smooth proper variety has weights in [-i,0], whereas its first homology V_p(A) has weights 0 and 1.
conventions.frobenius: For k=F_(p^f), phi is sigma-semilinear and only phi^f has a characteristic polynomial over K0. Arithmetic Frobenius on a Tate module is compared with geometric Frobenius on H^1 and with phi^f on crystalline H^1. The arithmetic Weil-Deligne Frobenius on D_st is phi^(-f), with the R06.3 descent factor for potentially semistable objects.
conventions.models: Mathlib reduction predicates include minimality; use a minimal equation. No integral lattice equality is inferred from a rational comparison. Good, semistable and potentially semistable are three different hypotheses.
